blocks.content: The Central Vigilance Commission is an independent body which is free from executive control in the exercise of its powers and functions.

rows: Strictly ineligible for any Central/State government post
Members eligible for UPSC Chairmanship; Chairman ineligible for government posts

items: Tenure Exception: The CVC tenure is 4 years (or 65 years of age), unlike standard statutory or constitutional bodies which usually have a 5 or 6-year tenure.
Further Employment Ban: Members are strictly ineligible for any further employment under the Central or State Governments post-retirement.
Removal Process: The President can remove the CVC on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity only after a Supreme Court inquiry.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Vigilance Commission is an independent body that functions free from executive control in performing its duties.
Members are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, Minister of Home Affairs, and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
The Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners hold office for a term of 4 years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
To ensure independence, members are not eligible for reappointment or further employment under the Central or State Governments after demitting office.
Salaries, allowances, and service conditions of the CVC are aligned with those of the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission.
